title: Arranging for Earl Hines, Erskine Tate and others after 1931
summary: Between the bands he arranged and gigged, with Earl Hines as a main customer and also Erskine Tate, Clyde Snyder and stage-show acts at the Regal.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, I guess to get things in proper order here, the '31 band broke up. And then, what did you do? I know in '33 Louis contacted you again. But what did you do in between?
In '31? Oh, well, I arranged music and played gigs. Went back to just arranging and playing, and one of my main customers was Earl Hines.
Now, he had the band at the Grand Terrace.
Yes. I arranged for Earl Hines then. And then I was arranger for others. And --
Who were some of the others, do you recall?
Earl Hines, and -- I don't know whether it was Chummy. I think he's dead, Chummy Cogg and Erskine Tate, yeah, Erskine Tate. He's still around, isn't he? Erskine Tate.
He may be, but if he is, he's quite
Yeah, he's -- well, I arranged for Erskine, and --
Did you have any dealings with Dave Paton?
Yes, I played at -- not at, but I played the Regal when they had the stage shows, and we had -- what did we have? Blackstone. We had Blackstone, the --
Magician. And Dave was playing. Dave had the band there. And -- oh, yes, and I arranged for Clyde Snyder. I done some arranging for Clyde Snyder and doing a lot of arranging for different acts.
